# Document parsing (Docling)

Converts PDFs into per-page Markdown, extracted figures, lossless Docling
JSON, and a quality/skip manifest — ready for a later LLM field-extraction
step (not included here).

## Setup

```bash
uv venv .venv-parsing
source .venv-parsing/bin/activate
uv pip install -r requirements-parsing.txt
cp .env.example .env.local   # then paste OPENAI_API_KEY + OPENAI_VISION_MODEL
```

```bash
# Cost estimate only (no OpenAI calls)
python -m parsing.run --pdf path/to/report.pdf --pages 1-20 --dry-run

# Parse without captions
python -m parsing.run --pdf path/to/report.pdf --pages 1-20 --no-captions --out output/

# Full parse with vision captions (requires .env.local)
python -m parsing.run --pdf path/to/report.pdf --pages 1-20 --out output/
```

Outputs land in `output/<doc_name>/`:

- `pages/pNNN.md` — one Markdown file per page
- `full.md` — non-skipped pages concatenated with page markers
- `document.json` — Docling lossless JSON
- `manifest.json` — per-page stats, `skipped`, quality flags
- `images/pNNN_figNN.png` — extracted figures
- `page_images/pNNN.png` — full-page renders for quality-flagged pages only

```bash
source .venv-parsing/bin/activate
pytest -q
```

## Project status

### Build health: green
`main` compiles clean (tsc, lint, production build all pass), confirmed live in browser across all 4 pages.

### What's real and working
- **Data**: 13,771 real BMW feedback rows (F70/G60/G70) + sales volumes + customer-study benchmarks, committed to the repo (`src/data/*.json`) so the whole team shares identical numbers
- **Landing page**: light theme, 3D Sketchfab car viewer (rotatable, color picker, interior/exterior toggle), vehicle switcher across all 3 lines, real per-component workflow status
- **PM workflow page**: light theme, requirement cards (approve/reject/postpone/challenge), sensitivity view (rank-fragility table), stakeholder matrix (reviewer × requirement grid), evidence/signal breakdown, audit trail
- **Stakeholder review page**: still dark theme, fully functional — customer-study chart, review submission
- **Evidence Explorer**: still dark theme, fully functional — filterable table over all 13,771 rows
- **Docker Compose**: local dev stack added (teammate's PR)
- **Docling PDF pipeline**: Python pipeline for better equipment-PDF parsing, built but not yet wired into the main ingestion flow

### Merged PRs (4, all green)
1. Landing page UI (3D viewer)
2. Document-parsing pipeline (Docling)
3. Workflow UI changes (light theme) — **landed broken** (3 files missing), I rebuilt and fixed them same-day
4. Docker Compose

### Open/in-progress
- **`evidence-UI-changes`** branch exists on remote but has **zero commits** — pushed but no work started yet. Likely a teammate about to light-theme the Evidence Explorer.

### By role
| Role | Status |
|---|---|
| **A (Backend/Data)** | Real ingestion pipeline done, deterministic scoring done. Docling parsing built but not integrated. Live in-app ingestion endpoint and web enrichment still open. |
| **B (AI/OpenAI)** | **Not started.** No `openai` package, no `.env.local`, all 6 `ai.ts` functions still mocked. Biggest gap in the project right now. |
| **C (PM frontend)** | My queue is clear — car viewer, sensitivity view, stakeholder matrix all shipped. Blocked items (pipeline live-progress, market switcher) wait on Role A. |
| **D (Stakeholder/trust)** | Base pages work; CSV export, dedicated audit view, low-confidence queue still open. Possibly starting now via `evidence-UI-changes`. |

### Known open items
- Light/dark theme split: landing + workflow = light; stakeholder + evidence = dark
- No OpenAI integration yet — this is the single biggest risk to the demo narrative (the "AI re-assesses a challenge" moment is still templated text, not live)
- Multi-market workflow support not built

**If I had to name the one thing most worth doing next**: get Role B started. Everything else is either done or waiting on something — the AI layer is the one piece nobody's touched, and it's the part judges will most want to see actually reasoning live.

Mapping current reality against the brief's own asks and the judges' evaluation criteria:

## 1. The three things judges explicitly want to see

| Ask | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **AI supporting identification, formulation, prioritization** | 🟡 Partial | Identification/formulation/prioritization *logic* is real and automated — but it's deterministic code (`deriveRequirements.ts`), not an LLM. No actual AI model has touched this pipeline yet. The "AI" in the demo narrative is currently scripted text, not live reasoning. |
| **Representative requirements with clear evidence/reasoning** | 🟢 Strong | Genuinely real: 13,771 actual BMW verbatims, real sales data, real customer-study benchmarks, every score factor has a cited rationale. This is the strongest part of the submission. |
| **Transparent decision support (review/challenge/modify/approve/reject, full traceability)** | 🟢 Strong mechanically, 🟡 weak on the "AI" part | Approve/reject/postpone/challenge all work, required rationale enforced, full audit log. But the Challenge button's "AI re-assesses" response is a template, not a real re-assessment — so the single most judge-visible "wow moment" in the brief isn't actually live yet. |

## 2. Evaluation criteria, one by one

| Criterion | Status | Reality check |
|---|---|---|
| **Decision and scoring logic** | 🟢 Strong | 7 real factors, 3 genuinely computed from data (frequency, sales_relevance, evidence_strength), 2 still heuristic placeholders (competitive_gap, strategic_fit), 1 intentionally unestimated (effort). Live-adjustable weights + sensitivity view showing rank fragility — this is a genuinely good demo of the criterion. |
| **Workflow and human decision-making** | 🟢 Strong | Full pipeline stages, PM actions, stakeholder matrix, reviewer disagreement surfaced. Solid. |
| **Traceability and auditability** | 🟢 Strong | Append-only log, actor+timestamp+old/new+rationale on every entry, AI vs human distinguished. Evidence Explorer adds a second traceability layer down to the raw verbatim. |
| **Solution quality, usability, feasibility** | 🟢 Strong, 🟡 one visible flaw | Light-theme landing/workflow pages look genuinely polished (3D viewer, real KPIs). But stakeholder page + Evidence Explorer are still dark theme — a judge clicking all four pages will notice the inconsistency. |
| **Innovation, scalability, business impact** | 🟡 Depends entirely on the pitch | The real differentiator here (BMW's own VFC taxonomy as pre-clustering instead of asking an LLM to cluster 14k verbatims from scratch) is a genuinely good scalability story — but only if it's told. Said nowhere in the live product itself; it's a talking point, not something a judge sees by clicking around. |

## 3. The one gap that matters most

**No OpenAI integration exists at all** — no package installed, no `.env.local`, all 6 AI functions in `ai.ts` are still deterministic mocks. Everything currently labeled "AI" in the UI (decision-trail summaries, challenge re-assessment, stakeholder overview) is seeded template text computed once at data-ingest time, not generated live.

This is the single biggest risk against judging criterion #1 and the brief's headline ask ("AI-powered application"). Right now, a technically sharp judge who asks "show me the AI actually thinking" would discover there isn't one running — everything they're seeing is either real deterministic math (good) or pre-written narrative (defensible as v0, but not what was asked for).

**If one thing gets done before demo time, it should be `summarizeDecisionTrail()` and `reassessChallenge()` going live against OpenAI** — those two are the functions a judge will actually trigger by clicking Challenge, and right now that click produces a canned response.

[Image: source: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-navneetkishansrinivasan-Desktop-ehl-alpha/cb8c26e5-1642-4704-9388-fdb98b1aa032/images/5.webp]

This is intentional, not a bug — here's exactly where it comes from and why it's identical across stakeholders.

## Where the data comes from

- **Customer-study charts** ("Easy to read and use instruments...", etc.) — `src/data/customer-study.json`, generated by `scripts/ingest-real-data.ts` from the real `F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx` file. Served by `GET /api/workflows/[id]/customer-study`, which matches the workflow's component (here, "Steering & Cockpit") to relevant customer-study categories via a keyword map in `deriveRequirements.ts`.
- **Requirement cards + score factors** ("227 verbatims mention Handling/Riding...", the 7-factor bars) — from `src/data/signals.json`/`feedback.json`, computed deterministically by `buildScoreFactors()` in the same file. This is the real verbatim-derived scoring I built earlier.

## Why it's the same for every stakeholder

Because none of this is scoped to the stakeholder at all — it's scoped to the **workflow** (component × vehicle × market). Look at the fetch calls in `src/app/stakeholder/[workflowId]/[stakeholderId]/page.tsx`:

```ts
api.listRequirements(wf.id),       // workflow-scoped
api.getCustomerStudy(wf.id),       // workflow-scoped
```

Neither takes `stakeholderId`. The `stakeholderId` param only controls two things on this page: which reviews get filtered into "Your review" at the bottom, and the "Signed in as" label. Everything above that — the evidence, the charts, the score breakdown — is the shared review packet every reviewer sees, by design: it's the same brief the PM is asking all 4 stakeholders to react to, so Engineering, Sales, Design, and Legal are all looking at identical evidence when they each give their opinion. Only their written opinion and approve/reject decision differ.

If you wanted this to genuinely differ per stakeholder (e.g. Design only sees design-relevant requirements, Legal only sees legally-relevant ones), that'd be a real feature to build — filtering the requirement list by some relevance mapping to each stakeholder's `expertise` field. Is that what you're asking for, or were you just confirming this isn't a bug?

PR #9 (`feature/role-b-ai`) wired **real OpenAI calls** into the AI layer, built by someone who clearly read `docs/ROLE_B_AI.md` closely:

- **Graceful fallback is correctly implemented**: no API key → falls back to the same deterministic text we had before, no crash, no broken build. I verified this live — the app works perfectly right now without a key. content.text:
`model: "gpt-4.1"` in the audit trail — confirmed real, live, working end to end. Now, your actual question:

## Are there guardrails? Yes, but partial — here's exactly what exists and what doesn't

**What's genuinely in place** (I read the code, not guessing):
- **Every call is token-bounded**: 320–700 max completion tokens per call type, never unbounded generation
- **Timeouts**: 25s on the main AI layer, 60s on Pingu chat — nothing hangs forever
- **Retry limit**: `maxRetries: 1` on the OpenAI client — no silent retry storms
- **Tool-call loop is capped**: Pingu's agentic loop hard-stops at 4 rounds, then forces a plain-text answer instead of looping
- **Chat history is capped**: only the last 12 turns get sent, so a long conversation doesn't balloon token usage per request
- **Tool outputs are bounded**: max 25 groups, 5 verbatim examples (240 chars each), 12 chart categories/4 series — the model can't pull back huge payloads
- **Input truncation**: Pingu messages get sliced to 4000 chars server-side before even reaching the model
- **Graceful fallback everywhere**: if a call fails or times out, every function falls back to deterministic text rather than erroring out — you just saw this with the Frunk challenge test before the key was added

**What's genuinely missing** — real gaps, not me being cautious:
- **No per-user/per-IP rate limiting** on `/api/chat` (Pingu) or the challenge endpoint. Anyone hitting these repeatedly could run up real spend — fine for a local demo, not fine if this is ever exposed publicly.
- **No spend cap or budget ceiling** in the app itself. The only ceiling is whatever limit you set on the OpenAI key/project dashboard.
- **No auth** on any endpoint — same situation as the rest of the app, known and documented, not new.
- **Pingu's tool results feed back into the prompt** without sanitization — low risk here since the tools are read-only (no write/execute capability, just data queries), but worth knowing if you ever extend Pingu with a tool that *does* something.

**For a hackathon demo**: this is fine as-is — you're the only one hitting it, usage is bounded per-call, and nothing will silently spiral. **If this gets shown to judges on a shared/public URL**, I'd set a hard spend limit on the key itself (OpenAI dashboard → Settings → Limits) as the real safety net, since the app has no internal one.

PR opened: **[#13 — Add in-app walkthrough tutorial (? icon)](https://github.com/NavneetKishanS/ehl-alpha/pull/13)**

## What it does

A "?" icon in the top-right of every page (part of the shared `SiteHeader`) opens a 7-slide walkthrough built from **real screenshots of the live app** — including one slide that genuinely shows a live OpenAI-generated decision-trail summary from our test earlier. Covers the landing page, workflow page (nav, live AI summary, requirement scoring), stakeholder review (including the expertise filter), and the Evidence Explorer (including your new market filter).

Previous/Next, dot-jump, keyboard shortcuts (←/→/Esc), backdrop-click to close — all verified live. Build's clean, branch + PR per the convention.

One thing worth knowing: since this bundles screenshots that happen to include real AI output from testing, if you ever restyle a page materially, these slides will look stale — they're meant to be retaken (same filenames in `public/tutorial/`) rather than hand-edited.

Here's a ready-to-paste Gamma prompt. I kept it tight since you said minimal info — each slide is scoped to 2-3 bullets max, and slide 5 is deliberately just a handoff to the live demo rather than more content.

---

**Paste this into Gamma:**

```
Create a 5-slide pitch deck for a hackathon submission to BMW Group's "AI for Product
Decision Making" challenge. Audience: hackathon judges who will watch a live product
demo immediately after this deck, so keep every slide minimal — a few words per bullet,
no paragraphs. This deck exists to set context fast, not to explain the product in
detail; the demo does that.

Style: clean, dark, BMW-brand feel (BMW blue #1c69d4 as the single accent color on a
near-black or white background, pick one and stay consistent). Generous whitespace, big
confident type, minimal icons, no stock photography, no clutter. Think "internal BMW
engineering tool," not "startup pitch."

Slide 1 — Title
- Title: "Requirements Copilot"
- Subtitle: "AI-assisted customer requirements for the next-generation BMW 1/5/7 Series"
- One line: "BMW Group Hackathon — [team name]"

Slide 2 — The problem, in one breath
- Headline: "~1 billion customer data points. ~1,000 requirements. One car."
- 3 bullets max:
  - PMs must turn customer feedback, sales data, and competitive signals into
    defensible product requirements
  - That process needs to stay transparent, evidence-based, and PM-controlled — not a
    black box
  - We built the tool that does this, grounded in BMW's real data

Slide 3 — What makes this real (not a mockup)
- Headline: "Grounded in real BMW data, not synthetic examples"
- 4 short stat-style bullets (numbers prominent, like a dashboard):
  - 13,771 real customer verbatims across BMW 1/5/7 Series
  - Real sales volumes + customer-study benchmarks across EU/US/China
  - Scored deterministically from real data — not an LLM guessing
  - Live OpenAI reasoning layered on top for judgment calls and PM challenges

Slide 4 — How it works (3 views, one audit trail)
- Headline: "Three roles, one transparent decision trail"
- 3 short columns or bullets, one per role:
  - PM workflow — pipeline stages, explainable scoring, approve/reject/challenge
  - Stakeholder review — each reviewer sees only what's relevant to their domain
  - Evidence Explorer — every requirement traces back to the real verbatim it came from
- One closing line under all three: "Every decision, every AI call, every override —
  logged and auditable."

Slide 5 — Demo handoff
- Headline: "Let's see it live"
- No bullets, no content — just the headline, large, centered
- Optional small subtext: "Everything on the previous slide, running for real."

Keep total word count low across all 5 slides — this is a spoken pitch with a live demo
right after, not a standalone document. Do not add a 6th slide, agenda slide, or
"thank you" slide.
```

---

A couple of notes on why I shaped it this way:
- **Slide 3's stats** are the ones I'd actually lean on if a judge pushes back — they're the hardest-to-fake part of the submission (real data, not synthetic).
- **Slide 5 is intentionally empty** — it's a beat, not content, so you're not reading a slide while trying to open the demo.
- If you want, I can swap slide 4's framing to lead with the evaluation criteria language from the brief ("decision and scoring logic," "traceability and auditability") instead of the 3-role breakdown — that's a more judge-literal angle if you'd rather score-match than narrate.

Given 3 hours left, here's what I'd actually prioritize — ranked by (judge-visible impact) ÷ (build risk), not just novelty:

## Top pick: close the "web research" gap the brief explicitly asks for

The brief literally says *"ground your proposals in customer feedback, BMW product and sales data, **and relevant web research**."* Right now `competitive_gap` only compares BMW models against each other (internal customer-study data) — there's zero external/competitor grounding anywhere in the app, and it's the one thing we've openly documented as missing. A judge who reads the brief closely will notice this is the one box not checked.

**Fastest safe version** (~1h): hand-curate 6-10 real, citable public facts about competitor vehicles (e.g., a competitor's charging time, a published review score) into a small JSON file with real URLs, and wire them into the `competitive_gap` factor's rationale with actual citations — not a live web-search API call (too risky to debug with time left). This turns "we compare BMW to BMW" into genuine cross-brand grounding, which is the single most on-brief gap left.

## Second pick: a portfolio view across all 3 vehicle lines

Right now every view is scoped to one component's workflow. A "Top opportunities across the whole lineup" page — ranking all ~60+ real requirements across F70/G60/G70 by score — would be almost zero backend risk (pure aggregation over data that already exists) and gives judges a concrete, visual answer to "does this scale beyond one demo workflow," which is literally one of the 5 scoring criteria and currently only a pitch-deck claim, not something they can click into.

## Lower priority, skip given the time box
- Portfolio/trade-off optimizer under an effort budget — genuinely interesting but real build risk in the time left
- Export/Jira integration — not a "wow," save it
- A "regenerate live with your own argument" button on stage — fun but marginal over what Challenge already does

**My recommendation**: do the competitive-grounding fix first (closes a named gap, ~1h), then the portfolio view if time remains (~45min, high visual payoff). Want me to start on the competitive grounding?

2. **~10 min** — wire these into `competitiveGap()` in `deriveRequirements.ts` as a deterministic blend (real external fact when one exists for that component, falls back to the current internal cross-model comparison when it doesn't) — safer and faster than re-running the AI judgment-factors batch job against all 67 requirements
3. **~10-15 min** — test live, build check, commit + PR

Shipped: **[PR #15](https://github.com/NavneetKishanS/ehl-alpha/pull/15)**

## Your demo flow, verified live

1. On any requirement, click **"+ Tag reviewers"** → pick stakeholders → Send
2. Switch to that stakeholder via the role-switcher dropdown (top-right)
3. Their stakeholder page shows **"Awaiting your review"** with the real evidence snapshot
4. Write an opinion, hit Approve → confirmed persisted with `decision: "approve"`

This is the exact flow you described: **as a PM, tag relevant stakeholders → log in as them → verify and approve** — live, not pre-seeded.

**One honest caveat for your demo script**: this works on *existing* requirements (all real, derived from actual data) — not a truly-from-zero new workflow, since every component already has one from the real data (confirmed earlier, nothing left empty to "create new" on). If you want to show the "create new workflow" button too, just pick any component, click it, and immediately use "Tag reviewers" on one of its requirements — same story, just skip narrating the empty "Ingest" stage it starts on.

git add -A && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Add an on-demand AI overview to each theme in "What customers are saying"

Like a retail "AI review summary", but per real feedback theme: click a
theme (e.g. "Seats") to expand it, and a 2-3 sentence summary synthesizes
the actual quotes shown below it - not invented detail, only what's in
the real verbatims. Generated lazily (one call per theme, the first time
it's expanded), not precomputed for all ~550 real signals.

- ai.ts: summarizeSignalOverview() - fast model, deterministic fallback
  if the call fails, same AIText { text, model, live } contract as the
  rest of the AI layer.
- db.ts: cacheSignalOverview() persists the result on the Signal (so a
  second click, or a page reload, is free) and logs it to the audit
  trail like every other AI output in the app.
- POST /api/signals/:id/overview, idempotent - returns the cached
  overview if one already exists instead of regenerating.
- SignalBreakdown.tsx: per-row loading state, "AI overview" badge when
  live, a visibly distinct fallback label if the call ever fails.

Verified live: expanding "Seats" (105 real verbatims) showed a spinner,
then a real gpt-4.1-mini synthesis of the actual quotes - confirmed
persisted via the API and logged to the audit trail (targetType
"signal", a new value added since nothing tracked AI output at the
signal level before).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
